w: Vice President, Hon. Justin Malewezi, welcomed Swamishri.

The Vice President of Malawi, Hon. Justin Malewezi, honored and welcomed Swamishri in an assembly of 400 aspirants. In his blessings Swamishri stated, "It is said in the Vedas that we are all God’s children. So there should be no distinctions of religion, caste or country. The world is one family. By sustaining such feelings we will experience peace within ourselves and bring peace to others..."

God says to Naradji, "To my mind there is no one greater than the sant (holy sadhu)." But why is the sant the greatest? Because he communicates the true glory of God to man and inspires profound faith for Him. .

w: Thakorji and the throne were decorated with the tricolors of the Indian Flag and Rakhadis. After puja Swamishri hoisted the Indian flag and Police Commissioner Mr.Hunter hoisted the American flag. In the evening assembly children performed a 'Kucch Geet' (march). Swamishri explained the importance of Raksha Bandhan in his blessings. Thereafter the sadhus tied Rakhadis on the devotees.

The Three Keys to Development A Bal karyakar asked Swamishri, "Bapa! We run the Bal Mandal in our own way but would you like to give any special instructions?" Swamishri responded, "You should be aware in not creating any lapses in the children's academic studies. If they are weak then employ teachers for that particular subject. They should not fall back in their studies. And the parents should not feel that their children have lagged in their studies because of their attendance to the mandir." "Secondly, their health. Pay attention for their good health. Explain to them to give up eating outside in restaurants and hotels. "And thirdly, their character and satsang values. Introduce them to Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Narrate stories from Yogiji Maharaj's Bodh Katha and inspire them to do puja daily…" For the all-round development of children Swamishri lucidly highlighted the three essential aspects of education, health and Satsang.
A karyakar is one who is wedded to faith, service and dedication.
To become a devotee of God is a great degree. To become a servant of God (sevak) is also a degree. So we should attain such degrees.

One liked by God will be liked by everyone, but one not liked by God will not be liked by anyone. And such a person will not attain virtues and be able to do good works. Therefore mould a life that pleases God.
God's commands (agna) are like jewellery; the more you wear it the more your splendor and greatness.

The deities were attired for the Independence Day celebration. After arti Swamishri came to the mandir ground for the flag hoisting ceremony. When Swamishri arrived with Thakorji on the ceremonial stage, children sang "Vande Mataram". Then Swamishri unfolded the Indian flag. More than 3,000 children and devotees saluted and offered respects to the flag. Then everyone sang the national anthem and concluded with 'Bharat Mata ki Jai' and the Jais of Sahajanand Swami and Guru parampara. Swamishri then addressed the gathering, "Today it is 15th August, India's Independence Day. We have celebrated this day in the mandir in the presence of God. Let us pray to God this day that there be peace in India. May there be an increase in moral feelings in people. We, as the citizens of India, are one. May all be inspired with feelings of harmony, friendliness and unity preached by Yogiji Maharaj. May all the small and big problems and difficulties of India be resolved. May all leaders of our country be blessed with good thoughts and intellect. We pray to Maharaj that there be peace in all parts of India. "May the teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the principles of India, our culture and spirituality spread day by day and people become awakened to it all. "We pray to Maharaj to do away with addictions, vices and ill-feelings and inspire feelings of faith and morality. May there be peace in our country and in Gujarat. May the fear in the minds of people dissolve."
In the evening assembly, an impressive drama, 'Paksh', showed Shri Krishna's effort in explaining the Kauravas to avoid the Mahabharat war.
Today was India's Independence Day. Before his morning puja, Swamishri performed the traditional flag-raising ceremony. Then he blessed the devotees with a special Independence Day message.

Early in the morning, Swamishri, sadhus, and devotees gathered in front of the mandir for the Dhvaj Vandan - flag raising ceremony - on India's Independence day, where all present saluted the Indian flag and sung the national anthem.

During the evening, the Midwest Satsang mandal performed the 'Sanskruti' programme. Through a combination of speeches, dances, dramas, and multimedia presentations, kishores portrayed the inventions, discoveries, and ideas of ancient Indian thinkers and spiritual masters. Senior sadhus also addressed the assembly, explaining the importance of preserving sanskruti as well as cultivating character. At the conclusion of the assembly, Swamishri said in his blessings that one must develop ideal characteristics like compassion, nonviolence, etc. He also stated that the purpose of having this human body is to become brahmarup and worship God. Finally, he stressed the importance of the holy Sadhu by saying that the Sadhu does not live for himself, but for the good of all. Earlier in the day, physicians and other healthcare professionals participated in a Medico-Spiritual Conference held in the presence of Swamishri.

Today marked India’s 59th Independence Day anniversary. Swamishri arrived on stage for his morning puja. The Nadiad Yuvak Mandal band greeted Swamishri as he arrived. Then Swamishri unfurled the Indian national flag, following which the national anthem was sung. After the formalities were over, Swamishri, still standing, blessed the devotees, “Today we pray to Maharaj that India progresses tremendously in the coming years. May there be peace throughout India. May there be goodwill towards all. May the country’s leaders also be blessed to serve well. May the country remain united. May India’s relations with the surrounding countries be peaceful. May relations with the rest of the world also be cordial. Dharma is our foundation. Life without dharma is not life85 we have to preserve the culture and traditions we have inherited. Values, dharma, knowledge, detachment and bhakti are all eternal. Such values and culture are our life. If God becomes our life, then true peace and happiness is possible.”

On India’s 62nd Independence Day celebration Tyagvallabh Swami unfurled the Indian flag. Then the entire congregation sang the national anthem. A one-day camp was arranged for all kishores and kishoris. About 3,500 teenagers had assembled in the mandir precincts. Swamishri was garlanded on the occasion and blessed all with his darshan.

To celebrate India’s Independence Day the flag hoisting ceremony was performed by Tyagvallabh Swami on the grounds of Bochasan Mandir. Then Viveksagar Swami spoke on independence. On Swamishri’s arrival youths of Borsad Satsang Chapter sang a song of national pride, “ Sãre jahã se achchhã. ” Swamishri waved the national flag. In conclusion, Tyagvallabh Swami garlanded Swamishri. The murtis in all the sanctums of the mandir were adorned in the tricolours.
Firm faith

3 August 2010, Bochasan A devotee revealed in his letter to Swamishri that he had met an astrologer because his business had run down. The astrologer gave him a horse shoe to keep in his home for a week. But there was no improvement. After that the devotee felt remorse for having lapsed in his faith. He wrote that he had breached his faith in him and requested for atonement ( prayaschit ). Swamishri replied, “Be vigilant and strong that you do not lapse again. Whatever happens believe it to be the wish of Shriji Maharaj. He wishes well for you.”
Social sanction

4 August 2010, Bochasan A youth from abroad called Swamishri. He revealed, “Swami I have fallen in love with a girl, and I wish to marry her. But the problem is that her parents wish to marry her to someone else.” Then he added, “If one is to have a love marriage where is the need of marrying someone of the same caste! Isn’t that right? In context to spiritual knowledge there are no distinctions of caste and class.” Swamishri broke into peals of laughter at his preaching. He replied, “You seem to be a great jnani .” Then Swamishri explained to him in a spirit of friendship, “If you are knowledgeable and wise then so am I. Now listen to me. If the girl’s parents give their consent and blessings then you can marry her. If the girl wishes to marry you, then she will do so. Do it with the consent of your parents and hers too.”Swamishri always upholds systems and traditions that have social sanction and the authority of the Hindu shastras.
Near and far

12 August 2010, Bochasan Swamishri communicates and blesses devotees on a personal level either through his daily audience session, letters or by phone. In spite of his advanced age, Swamishri is still active and responds punctually to the enquiries from devotees on mundane and spiritual matters. Just as he answers the youths and devotees he equally appreciates and responds to children. Akhand, a little boy in America, asked Swamishri on the phone, “Where are you?” Swamishri replied, “I am in Bochasan and with you too!”Swamishri’s brief answer conveyed the depth of Hindu theology that God and his Sadhu are all-pervading and present wherever their devotees reside.
Happiness in all situations
13 August 2010, Bochasan
After his brief afternoon walk Swamishri was about to lie down to rest on his bed. At that time Bhagvatcharan Swami remarked, “You are very happy.”

Swamishri spoke with pride, “I have the association of God, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Is there any greater happiness other than them in this world! If one realizes this then no matter in illness or good health, in insult or honour, there is always happiness, happiness and happiness!"

st.t: United States Congressional Delegation Strengthens Cultural Exchange
w: A distinguished United States Congressional Delegation led by Congressman Ro Khanna (CA-17) and Congressman Michael Waltz (FL-06), co-chairs of the bipartisan Congressional Caucus on India and Indian Americans, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi.

The delegation leaders and Congresswoman Deborah Ross (NC-2) and Congresswoman Kat Cammack (FL-3) were traditionally welcomed. Then they paid their respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and admired its art and architecture. They gained insights into the significance of the temple’s design elements and spiritual philosophy.

The US congressional delegation also performed ‘abhishek,’ to pray for peace and best wishes. Experiencing the cultural boat ride through thousands of years of Indian history also left a lasting impression of India’s rich heritage.

Congressman Ro Khanna expressed his gratitude, “We are honored to have been graciously welcomed by the Akshardham community. This visit has strengthened our nations’ friendship bonds and highlighted the significance of cultural exchange.”

Congressman Michael Waltz remarked, “Our visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham has been an incredible experience that deepened our understanding of India’s cultural and spiritual roots. The warm reception and the opportunity to partake in sacred rituals have left a lasting impression on our delegation.”
